cells.description: “I’m interested in opening up the possibilities we access as performers when improvising. The Careful Scientist task is designed to challenge habitual patterns of coordination and attention as are many of our training exercises. But this one focuses on working alone without an external trigger and performing different actions simultaneously on two sides of the body.” Thomas Hauert

cells.title: Habit CallOutText1
cells.description: “The body has a tendency to follow known paths. In order to increase our movement vocabularies to include as many of the countless possibilities that the human body allows, we have devised exercises to surpass the movement patterns that have become habitual.”

additional_fields.html-content:

cells.title: Habit BodyText 6
cells.description: “The body has a tendency to stop one action when starting a new action. With this exercise and others, we are interested in training ourselves to continue a particular task even while our attention is busy initiating another movement, something like juggling.”

additional_fields.html-content:
“All of our strategies to practice and invent movement are somehow about priming the intuition. I understand intuition as a neuro-physiological phenomenon that relies on our experience and our memory, enabling us to act without needing to process it first.”
----- Thomas Hauert

cells.title: Habit Body Text 2
cells.description: Thomas Hauert and Zoo Company’s have developed an exercise they call the Careful Scientist that uses a very tight set of rules to complicate the coordination between limbs across the two sides of the body. The ultimate goal of this exercise is to translate the intricate combinations it produces to any joint of the body including the joints in the fingers, toes, and the chain of the spine.

cells.title: Habit Body Text 4
cells.description:
The Careful Scientist Exercise consists of a very limited set of four actions in certain joints of the upper body. Usually it is practiced lying on the floor, but it can also be done standing. 
The goal is to teach the body to execute two of these four movements simultaneously in the left and right arm using the following constraints:

Avoid symmetry and opposites in the two arms to:

Execute different actions on the left and right simultaneously

Build up to overlapping timing on the two sides of the body by initially starting and stopping both sides at the same time and then eventually working up to overlapping motion (change the actions in both arms at different times, so that the action in one arm continues while the other changes). 

Work to add complexity by changing durations and amplitudes for the different movements, trying to separate all these parameters left and right.

After practicing the upper body, movements in the legs, hips and knees can be added for a greater challenge.

additional_fields.html-content:
Rules for the Careful Scientist Exercise
The Careful Scientist Exercise consists of a very limited set of four actions in certain joints of the upper body. Usually it is practiced lying on the floor, but it can also be done standing. The goal is to teach the body to execute two of these four movements simultaneously in the left and right arm using the following constraints.

Avoid symmetry and opposites in the two arms to:

1. Execute different actions on the left and right simultaneously.

2. Build up to overlapping timing on the two sides of the body by initially starting and stopping both sides at the same time and then eventually working up to overlapping motion (change the actions in both arms at different times, so that the action in one arm continues while the other changes).

3. Work to add complexity by changing durations and amplitudes for the different movements, trying to separate all these parameters left and right.

4. After practicing the upper body, movements in the legs, hips, and knees can be added for a greater challenge.

cells.title: Habit Body Text 1
cells.description: Thomas Hauert’s creative process often begins from an investigation of the workings of the locomotor system and, in particular, the joints, those points of articulation between bones that allow changes in spatial relationship to occur. In this aspect of his work, Thomas is focusing his investigations on the way our joints move, their ranges of motion, and the programmed coordinations between them. He and his dancers work to become aware of habits from daily life or training and to devise tasks to retrain or restrain those habits and expand the palette of possibilities.
